proposed_from.topic: Feedback-core exact-risk certification for weighted random isolation. Revive banked parent exp_awri_mixture_minimax_certificate with a different mathematical angle: given its fixed WRI/RDIM network-design model and a supplied size-k feedback vertex set of the conflict graph, prove an evaluated cutoff-forest moment algebra that computes every one/two-tagged greedy-isolated-set count polynomial and dense rational RDIM risk matrix in L n^2 2^{O(k log(k+1))} poly(n,b,lambda) bit operations, with no (nb)^k table or unevaluated integration gate. Use the derived 3^k core inclusion-exclusion reduction, complete vertex-cover oracle, and ordered-ratio nested-moment recurrence as traction; close heterogeneous forest branching, moving boundary integration, all tags, and intermediate bit height. Then return a rational epsilon-minimax primal-dual certificate for the finite rule library; omit the parent's unsupported exact algebraic optimizer. Consumer: exact AWRI rule selection for a rural-China insurance-diffusion follow-up after measuring the conflict graph's feedback number. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A three-state cutoff-forest reduction and exact core inclusion-exclusion identity were derived; vertex-cover cores are FPT, and a directed-realizable feedback-k family with binomial dense support has an O(k! k m^2) nested-ratio evaluation. Exact checks matched all 44 C6 tag polynomials, 288 risk entries, 384 vertex-cover queries, six repeated-star cases, and three heterogeneous cases. Relative core order and scalar activation counts both failed, while no prior-art collision or universal obstruction was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove an evaluated moment representation for heterogeneous cutoff-forest messages that preserves future core-priority exponent profiles and closes under branching, component products, moving-endpoint integration, and tagged coefficient extraction in true FPT bit complexity. EARLY KILL TEST: On heterogeneous replicated-star integrals with k<=3, m<=2, and branch weights in {1,2}, match all tags and the private-leaf encoding to exact residual enumeration and prove symbolic arbitrary-k,m complexity; if closure still indexes k degree totals or profile-count vectors with an n-dependent exponent, stop and pivot before general forest or SDP work. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest design paper is Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li: it fixes the WRI and RDIM objects but replaces analytical evaluation of its risk surrogate by simulation. The closest combinatorial papers are Pippenger and Gamarnik--Goldberg, whose tree recursions target scalar occupation or limiting expected size, and Wan, Tu, Zhang, and Li, whose dynamic program counts static independent sets. None evaluates the finite heterogeneous priority measure after conditioning on a feedback core, preserves every one- and two-tagged count coefficient, proves polynomial intermediate rational height, and reconstructs the dense RDIM risk matrix in fixed-parameter bit complexity. Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje optimize over all designs and estimators through a different implicit conflict-graph functional; the present kernel makes no claim to compute or tighten that unrestricted minimax value. Its theorem concerns an exact, prespecified WRI and RDIM library. The bounded searches covered the exact target--method pair and adjacent priority-order, treewidth, random sequential adsorption, and network-design literatures; no closer result subsuming the kernel was located.

seed_details.title: Evaluated feedback-core algebra for exact WRI and RDIM risk
seed_details.anchor_location: Algorithm 3, Theorem 4.1, Appendix S2.1, Section 4.2, and Section 6
seed_details.opened_evidence: Algorithm 3 fixes weighted sequential random isolation; Theorem 4.1 and Appendix S2.1 bound RDIM mean squared error by balance and reciprocal-size terms; Section 4.2 simulates the resulting surrogate because its analytical evaluation is complicated; Section 6 asks for stronger theory and effective probability approximation.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Conditioning on a supplied feedback set creates numerical core cutoffs in otherwise independent forest components. The missing theorem is an evaluated representation that closes under heterogeneous child products, moving endpoints, component products, and every tag while avoiding a table with an exponent depending on \(k\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the scalar time-indexed occupation message used on a tree by a core-conditioned operator message that preserves the future ordered-ratio exponent profile when distinct branches attach to distinct subsets of the core.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining weighted random isolation, greedy maximal independent sets, feedback vertex number, exact tagged moments, and priority-order integration found tree occupation recursions and static bounded-treewidth counting, but no exact weighted tagged greedy-law algorithm parameterized by feedback vertex number.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from bounded-treewidth dynamic programming because independent sets and their size polynomial are already fixed-parameter tractable.
seed_details.rebuttal: Static independent-set counts assign one weight per set, whereas WRI assigns the total probability mass of all priority orders producing that set; heterogeneous core cutoffs retain numerical order information that ordinary bag states discard.

seed_details.title: Rational near-minimax certificate for a finite WRI rule library
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the informal main result, Section 6, Appendix A, and Conclusion
seed_details.opened_evidence: The paper makes the conflict graph the design-based minimax object and bounds the unrestricted design-and-estimator risk; its Introduction calls the exact graph functional complicated, while its Conclusion identifies computational complexity as open. It does not give a rational certificate for a prespecified WRI and RDIM library.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Given exact rational rule matrices, turn the ellipsoidal worst-case risk into primal and dual spectral epigraphs and return rational feasible points with a directly checkable gap, without asserting that an exact optimizer is rational.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the unsupported exact real-algebraic optimizer by weak rational semidefinite optimization, strict-feasibility erosion, affine repair, and outward objective rounding.
seed_details.destination_search: Kallus supplies the zero-sum role of mixed experimental designs, Duarte, Sagnol, and Wong supply semidefinite minimax-design machinery, and Groetschel, Lovasz, and Schrijver supply weak rational convex optimization; none begins with exact WRI and RDIM risk matrices or emits this certificate.
seed_details.red_team: Once the matrices are known, this is merely a standard semidefinite program.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection limits its novelty, so the certificate is retained as a downstream deliverable rather than the tier-bearing kernel; its value is to make exact risk computation operational and independently auditable.

seed_details.title: Design-based RDIM limit law after graph-only WRI rule selection
seed_details.anchor_location: The seed named \(\texttt{seed-wri-limit-law}\), its first changed proof step, and the terminal scope discussion
seed_details.opened_evidence: The prior proposal records that conditioning on the isolated set leaves unresolved the unconditioning over a global greedy support and random reciprocal denominators. The source paper supplies simulation evidence but no studentized design-based central limit theorem.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Show that conditioning on finitely many feedback-core states localizes forest support changes strongly enough for a uniform conditional-to-unconditional central limit theorem and a conservative or consistent studentizer.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Before invoking a dependency-graph or Stein argument, prove a quantitative stabilization radius for WRI inclusion indicators after the core priorities and the graph-only selected rule are fixed.
seed_details.destination_search: Aronow and Samii prove asymptotic normality from local exposure dependence, Leung proves approximate-neighborhood-interference normality with network HAC inference, and Krivelevich, M\'esz\'aros, Michaeli, and Shikhelman prove local-limit control for random greedy independent sets; none covers RDIM with a generated weighted greedy support and random denominators after rule selection.
seed_details.red_team: Condition on the isolated set and apply the complete-randomization central limit theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The conditional centering varies with a globally selected and potentially unrepresentative support, and the random arm denominators can fail to stabilize; neither issue disappears after conditioning.

seed_details.title: Parameterized hardness of one risk-determining WRI coefficient
seed_details.anchor_location: General review improvement directive and the abandoned hardness seed in the proposal core
seed_details.opened_evidence: The prior review demands a parameter-preserving hardness reduction, while the prior seed admits that its poset flower does not encode greedy domination and provides no coefficient-recovery identity.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Construct a domination gadget whose single one- or two-tagged coefficient recovers a standard parameterized source count while the feedback vertex number depends only on the source parameter.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Translate a source order constraint into the existence of an earlier selected neighbor, rather than importing a poset comparability gadget that has no greedy-domination semantics.
seed_details.destination_search: The closest order-counting hardness result concerns cover-graph treewidth, not WRI feedback vertex number; no source problem and gadget with the required parameter map was located.
seed_details.red_team: Counting linear extensions is already hard at bounded cover-graph width, so the WRI claim follows.
seed_details.rebuttal: A priority order accepted by WRI is characterized by independent domination, not by transitive order constraints; without a reduction the comparator gives only warning, not hardness.
seed_details.disposition: dropped because the positive construction has substantially stronger traction

seed_details.title: Ordered-ratio closure for heterogeneous replicated-star integrals
seed_details.anchor_location: The feedback-core presolve, Sections 4 and 5.2, and the parent technical limitation
seed_details.opened_evidence: The presolve derives a directed-realizable replicated-star family with dense conditional support, proves a scalar ordered-ratio recurrence for identical attachments, and exhibits two heterogeneous profiles that defeat activation-count compression. The parent technical limitation states that finite width checks cannot establish fixed-parameter tractability.
seed_details.proof_boundary: For the directed-realizable replicated-star family, compress a product of heterogeneous core-coupled component factors into nested moments with state size depending only exponentially on \(k\) and polynomially on the number of branches.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace one scalar occupation message by an ordered-ratio operator that carries the full future prefix-weight profile created when a heterogeneous branch term activates.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found scalar or distributional tree recursions and exact one-dimensional adsorption laws, but no symbolic arbitrary-\(k,m\) evaluation of these heterogeneous core-boundary integrals.
seed_details.red_team: The ordered-ratio recurrence for identical attachments extends by simply recording the number of activated branches.
seed_details.rebuttal: Two branches with profiles \((1,1)\) and \((1,2)\) can have the same current activation count and exponent but different future exponents, so scalar activation is not a sufficient state.
seed_details.disposition: absorbed as the mandatory first test of the selected seed

seed_details.title: Exact evaluation of the published AWRI surrogate on feedback-small graphs
seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 4.1, Equation defining \(\mathcal M(\mathbf w)\), and Algorithm 4
seed_details.opened_evidence: The paper's selection rule minimizes a simulated degree-balance and reciprocal-arm-size surrogate over candidate weights. Its proof identifies exactly which isolated-set moments enter that surrogate.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Compute only the marked degree histogram and reciprocal arm-size terms, potentially permitting a smaller state than the dense RDIM risk matrix.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Monte Carlo averages in Algorithm 4 by tagged generating-function coefficients before asking for all pairwise RDIM moments.
seed_details.destination_search: No exact bounded-feedback evaluation of the published surrogate was located, although the full selected seed would make this result a corollary.
seed_details.red_team: The full tagged-risk oracle immediately contains every surrogate moment.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds once the selected theorem is proved; the narrower oracle is therefore not an independent paper kernel.

seed_details.title: Priority-weighted independent-set polynomial on bounded treewidth
seed_details.anchor_location: Abstract and main dynamic-programming result on pages 42--47
seed_details.opened_evidence: Wan, Tu, Zhang, and Li compute the number of independent sets of every size on a graph of treewidth \(p\) in \(O(2^p p n^3)\) time. Their objective is a static cardinality count and contains no priority-order probability.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Define and compute the generating polynomial whose coefficient weights each maximal independent set by the probability that heterogeneous greedy priorities produce it.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: At a separator forget operation, integrate the forgotten priority while retaining which boundary vertices can still dominate later vertices.
seed_details.destination_search: Order-counting work indicates that multivariate separator integration may remain only XP, and no matching FPT theorem for the priority-weighted polynomial was located.
seed_details.red_team: Attach the WRI probability as a local vertex weight in the existing independent-set polynomial.
seed_details.rebuttal: The probability of a maximal independent set is a sum over compatible global orders and does not factor into vertex weights, so the static recurrence cannot be reused unchanged.
seed_details.disposition: dropped because feedback-core conditioning gives a sharper tractable interface than general treewidth

seed_details.title: Robust WRI selection over an uncertain conflict graph
seed_details.anchor_location: Conclusion discussion of weighted, noisy, and unobserved social networks
seed_details.opened_evidence: The conclusion explicitly identifies network noise and nonobservation as practical limitations, whereas the WRI construction conditions on one fixed known network.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Optimize the exact worst-case risk over a compact family of edge completions whose members share a small feedback core.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Core-conditioned forest messages must propagate unresolved edge states jointly with priority cutoffs because each completion changes both feasibility and the greedy law.
seed_details.destination_search: Robust-network methods were found for sensitivity and averaging, but not an exact WRI risk separation oracle over exponentially many feedback-small graph completions.
seed_details.red_team: Compute every candidate graph separately and maximize the resulting risk.
seed_details.rebuttal: That enumerates exponentially many completions and supplies no compact certificate; current evidence is insufficient for a credible theorem route.

seed_details.title: Exact WRI risk when the supplied feedback core is a vertex cover
seed_details.anchor_location: Forest-oracle theorem and feedback-core presolve vertex-cover branch
seed_details.opened_evidence: The parent establishes exact forest messages, and the presolve derives direct chamber integration when deleting the core leaves an edgeless graph.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Enumerate independent core selections, blocker subsets, and core orders, then integrate the resulting chamber monomials.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Outside vertices become forced by the selected core, so no heterogeneous tree branching remains.
seed_details.destination_search: The complete derivation and finite exact checks already settle this special case inside the supplied presolve evidence.
seed_details.red_team: This is no longer an open research seed because the supplied derivation already gives the algorithm.
seed_details.disposition: dropped and retained only as a theorem-level boundary check
